subject: Manifesto

matches.quote:
The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for
the human race. They have greatly increased the life-expectancy of those
of us who live in "advanced" countries, but they have destabilized
society, have made life unfulfilling, have subjected human beings to
indignities, have led to widespread psychological suffering (in the Third
World to physical suffering as well) and have inflicted severe damage on
the natural world. The continued development of technology will worsen the
situation. It will certainly subject human beings to greater indignities
and inflict greater damage on the natural world, it will probably lead to
greater social disruption and

and it may lead to increased
physical suffering even in "advanced" countries

The industrial-technological system may survive or it may break down.
If it survives, it MAY eventually achieve a low level of physical and
psychological suffering, but only after passing through a long and very
painful period of adjustment and only at the cost of permanently reducing
human beings and many other living organisms to engineered products and
mere cogs in the social machine. Furthermore, if the system survives, the
consequences will be inevitable: There is no way of reforming or modifying
the system so as to prevent it from depriving people of dignity and
autonomy

If the system breaks down the consequences will still be very painful.
But the bigger the system grows the more disastrous the results of its
breakdown will be, so if it is to break down it had best break down sooner
rather than later

We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system. This
revolution may or may not make use of violence; it may be sudden or it may
be a relatively gradual process spanning a few decades. We can't predict
any of that. But we do outline in a very general way the measures that
those who hate the industrial system should take in order to prepare the
way for a revolution against that form of society. This is not to be a
POLITICAL revolution. Its object will be to overthrow not governments but
the economic and technological basis of the present society

In this article we give attention to only some of the negative
developments that have grown out of the industrial-technological system.
Other such developments we mention only briefly or ignore altogether. This
does not mean that we regard these other developments as unimportant. For
practical reasons we have to confine our discussion to areas that have
received insufficient public attention or in which we have something new
to say. For example, since there are well-developed environmental and
wilderness movements, we have written very little about environmental
degradation or the destruction of wild nature, even though we consider
these to be highly important.


THE PSYCHOLOGY OF 
MODERN LEFTISM

Almost everyone will agree that we live in a deeply troubled society.
One of the most widespread manifestations of the craziness of our world is
leftism, so a discussion of the psychology of leftism can serve as an
introduction to the discussion of the problems of modern society in
general

But what is leftism? During the first half of the 20th century leftism
could have been practically identified with socialism. Today the movement
is fragmented and it is not clear who can properly be called a leftist.
When we speak of leftists in this article we have in mind mainly
socialists, collectivists, "politically correct" types, feminists, gay and
disability activists, animal rights activists and the like. But not
everyone who is associated with one of these movements is a leftist. What
we are trying to get at in discussing leftism is not so much

movement or
an ideology as a psychological type, or rather a collection of related
types. Thus, what we mean by "leftism" will emerge more clearly in the
course of our discussion of leftist psychology. (Also, see paragraphs

Even so, our conception of leftism will remain a good deal less clear
than we would wish, but there doesn't seem to be any remedy for this. All
we are trying to do

is indicate in a rough and approximate way the
two psychological tendencies that we believe are the main driving force of
modern leftism. We by no means claim to be telling the WHOLE truth about
leftist psychology. Also, our discussion is meant to apply to modern
leftism only. We leave open the question of the extent to which our
discussion could be applied to the leftists of the 19th and early 20th

The two psychological tendencies that underlie modern leftism we call
"feelings of inferiority" and "oversocialization." Feelings of inferiority
are characteristic of modern leftism as a whole, while oversocialization
is characteristic only of a certain segment of modern leftism; but this
segment is highly influential.


FEELINGS OF
INFERIORITY

By "feelings of inferiority" we mean not only inferiority feelings in
the

sense but a whole spectrum of related traits; low self-esteem,
feelings of powerlessness, depressive tendencies, defeatism, guilt,
self-hatred, etc. We argue that modern leftists tend to have

such
feelings (possibly more or less repressed) and that these feelings are
decisive in determining the direction of modern leftism

When someone interprets as derogatory almost anything that is said
about him (or about groups with whom he identifies) we conclude that he
has inferiority feelings or low self-esteem. This tendency is pronounced
among minority rights

whether or not they belong to the
minority groups whose rights they defend. They are hypersensitive about
the words used to designate minorities

minorities. The terms "negro," "oriental," "handicapped" or
"chick" for an African, an Asian, a disabled person or a woman originally
had no derogatory connotation. "Broad" and "chick" were merely the
feminine equivalents of "guy," "dude" or "fellow." The negative
connotations have been attached to these terms by the activists
themselves. Some animal rights

have gone so far as to reject the
word "pet" and insist on its replacement by "animal companion

anthropologists go to great lengths to avoid saying anything about
primitive peoples that could conceivably be interpreted as negative. They
want to replace the

primitive" by "nonliterate." They seem almost
paranoid about anything that might suggest that any primitive culture is
inferior to our own. (We do not mean to imply that primitive cultures ARE
inferior to ours. We merely point out the hypersensitivity of leftish
anthropologists

Those who are most sensitive about "politically incorrect" terminology
are not the average black ghetto-dweller, Asian immigrant, abused woman or
disabled person, but a minority of activists, many of whom do not even
belong to any "oppressed" group but come from privileged strata of
society. Political correctness has its stronghold among university
professors, who have secure employment with comfortable salaries, and the
majority of whom are heterosexual white males from middle

Many leftists have an intense identification with the problems of
groups that have an image of being weak (women), defeated (American
Indians), repellent (homosexuals) or otherwise inferior. The leftists
themselves feel that these groups are inferior. They would never admit

to
themselves that they have such feelings, but it is precisely because they
do see these groups as inferior that they identify with their problems.
(We do not

suggest that women, Indians, etc. ARE inferior; we are
only making a point about leftist psychology

Feminists are desperately anxious to prove that women are as strong
and as capable as men. Clearly they are nagged by a fear that women may
NOT be as strong and as capable as men

Leftists tend to hate anything that has an image of being strong, good
and successful. They hate America, they hate Western civilization, they
hate white males, they hate rationality. The reasons that leftists give
for hating the West, etc. clearly do not correspond with their real
motives. They SAY they hate the West because it is warlike, imperialistic,
sexist, ethnocentric and so forth, but where these same faults appear in
socialist countries or in primitive cultures, the leftist finds excuses
for them, or at best he GRUDGINGLY admits that they exist; whereas he
ENTHUSIASTICALLY points out (and often greatly exaggerates) these faults
where they appear in Western civilization. Thus it is clear that these
faults are not the leftist's real motive for hating America and the West.
He hates America and the West because they are strong and successful

Words like "self-confidence," "self-reliance," "initiative,"
"enterprise," "optimism," etc., play little role in the liberal and
leftist vocabulary. The leftist is anti-individualistic, pro-collectivist.
He wants society to solve everyone's

everyone's
needs for them, take care of them. He is not the sort of person who has an
inner sense of confidence in his

ability to solve his own problems and
satisfy his own needs. The leftist is antagonistic to the concept of
competition because, deep inside, he feels like a loser

intellectuals tend to focus on
sordidness, defeat and despair, or else they take an orgiastic tone,
throwing off rational control as if there were no hope of accomplishing
anything through rational calculation and all that was left was to immerse
oneself in the sensations of the moment

philosophers tend to dismiss reason, science, objective
reality and to insist that everything is culturally relative. It is true
that one can ask serious questions about the foundations of scientific
knowledge and about how, if at all, the concept of objective reality can
be defined. But it is obvious that modern

philosophers are not
simply cool-headed logicians systematically analyzing the foundations of
knowledge. They are deeply involved emotionally in their attack on truth
and reality. They attack these concepts because of their own psychological
needs. For one thing, their attack is an outlet for hostility, and, to the

OVERSOCIALIZATION

Psychologists use the term "socialization" to designate the process by
which children are trained to think and act as society demands. A person

may seem senseless to say that many leftists are

THE POWER PROCESS

Human beings have a need (probably based in biology) for something
that we will call the "power process." This is closely related to the need
for power (which is widely recognized) but is not quite the same thing.
The power process has four elements. The three most clear-cut of these we
call goal, effort and attainment of goal. (Everyone needs to have goals
whose attainment requires effort, and needs to succeed in attaining at
least some of his goals.) The fourth element is more difficult to define
and may not be necessary for everyone. We call it autonomy and will
discuss it later (paragraphs

Consider the hypothetical case of a man who can have anything he wants
just by wishing for it. Such a man has power, but he will develop serious
psychological problems. At first he will have a lot of fun, but by and by
he will become acutely bored and demoralized. Eventually he may become
clinically depressed. History shows that leisured aristocracies tend to
become decadent. This is not true of fighting aristocracies that have to
struggle to maintain their power. But leisured, secure aristocracies that
have no need to exert themselves usually become bored, hedonistic and
demoralized, even though they have power. This shows that power is not
enough. One must have goals toward which to exercise one's power

Everyone has goals; if nothing else, to obtain the physical
necessities of life: food, water and whatever clothing and shelter are
made necessary by the climate. But the leisured aristocrat obtains these
things without effort. Hence his boredom and demoralization

Nonattainment of important goals results in death if the goals are
physical necessities, and in frustration if nonattainment of the goals is
compatible with survival. Consistent failure to attain goals throughout
life results in defeatism, low self-esteem or depression

Thus, in order to avoid serious psychological problems, a human being
needs goals whose attainment requires effort, and he must have a
reasonable rate of success in attaining his goals.


SURROGATE ACTIVITIES

But not every leisured aristocrat becomes bored and demoralized. For
example, the emperor Hirohito, instead of sinking into decadent hedonism,
devoted himself to marine biology, a field in which he became
distinguished. When people do not have to exert themselves to satisfy
their physical needs they often set up artificial goals for themselves. In
many cases they then pursue these goals with the same energy and emotional
involvement that they otherwise would have put into the search for
physical necessities. Thus the aristocrats of the Roman Empire had their
literary

many European aristocrats a few centuries ago
invested tremendous time and energy in hunting, though they certainly
didn't need the meat; other aristocracies have competed for status through
elaborate displays of wealth; and a few aristocrats, like Hirohito, have
turned to science

We use the term "surrogate activity" to designate an activity that is
directed toward an artificial goal that people set up for themselves
merely in order to have some goal to work toward, or let us say, merely
for the sake of the "fulfillment" that they get from pursuing the goal.
Here is a rule of thumb for the identification of surrogate activities.
Given a person who devotes much time and energy to the pursuit of goal X,
ask yourself this: If he had to devote most of his time and energy to
satisfying his biological needs, and if that effort required him to use
his physical and mental

in a varied and interesting way, would
he feel seriously deprived because he did not attain goal X? If the answer
is no, then the person's pursuit of

goal X is a surrogate activity.
Hirohito's studies in marine biology clearly constituted a surrogate
activity, since it is pretty certain that if Hirohito had had to spend his
time working at interesting non-scientific tasks in order to obtain the
necessities of life, he would not have felt deprived because he didn't
know all about the anatomy and life-cycles of marine animals. On the other
hand the pursuit of sex and love (for example) is not a surrogate
activity, because most people, even if their existence were otherwise
satisfactory, would feel deprived if they passed their lives without ever
having a relationship with a member of the opposite sex. (But pursuit of
an excessive amount of sex, more than one really needs, can be a surrogate
activity

In modern industrial society only minimal effort is necessary to
satisfy one's physical needs. It is enough to go through a training
program to acquire some petty technical skill, then come to work on time
and exert

very modest effort needed to hold a job. The only
requirements are a moderate amount of intelligence and, most of all,
simple OBEDIENCE. If one has those, society takes care of one from cradle
to grave. (Yes, there is an underclass that cannot take

physical
necessities for granted, but we are speaking here of mainstream society.)
Thus it is not surprising that modern society is full of surrogate

humanitarian work, artistic and literary creation, climbing the corporate

example, the majority of scientists will probably agree that the
"fulfillment" they get from their work is more important than the money
and prestige they earn

For many if not most people, surrogate activities are less satisfying
than the pursuit of real goals (that is, goals that people would want to
attain even if their need for the power process were already fulfilled).
One indication of this is the fact that, in many or most cases, people who
are deeply involved in surrogate activities are never satisfied, never at

The scientist no sooner solves one problem than he moves on to the next.
The long-distance runner drives himself to run always farther and faster.
Many people who pursue surrogate activities will say that they get far

is because in our

autonomy in pursuing their surrogate activities

INDUSTRIAL SOCIETY AND 
ITS FUTURE


Introduction

1. The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for
the human race. They have greatly increased the life-expectancy of those
of us who live in "advanced" countries, but they have destabilized
society, have made life unfulfilling, have subjected human beings to
indignities, have led to widespread psychological suffering (in the Third
World to physical suffering as well) and have inflicted severe damage on
the natural world. The continued development of technology will worsen the
situation. It will certainly subject human beings to greater indignities
and inflict greater damage on the natural world, it will probably lead to
greater social disruption and psycholo and it may lead to increased
physical suffering even in "advanced" countries.
2. The industrial-technological system may survive or it may break down.
If it survives, it MAY eventually achieve a low level of physical and
psychological suffering, but only after passing through a long and very
painful period of adjustment and only at the cost of permanently reducing
human beings and many other living organisms to engineered products and
mere cogs in the social machine. Furthermore, if the system survives, the
consequences will be inevitable: There is no way of reforming or modifying
the system so as to prevent it from depriving people of dignity and
autonomy.
3. If the system breaks down the consequences will still be very painful.
But the bigger the system grows the more disastrous the results of its
breakdown will be, so if it is to break down it had best break down sooner
rather than later.
4. We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system. This
revolution may or may not make use of violence; it may be sudden or it may
be a relatively gradual process spanning a few decades. We can't predict
any of that. But we do outline in a very general way the measures that
those who hate the industrial system should take in order to prepare the
way for a revolution against that form of society. This is not to be a
POLITICAL revolution. Its object will be to overthrow not governments but
the economic and technological basis of the present society.
5. In this article we give attention to only some of the negative
developments that have grown out of the industrial-technological system.

does not mean that we regard these other developments as unimportant. For
practical reasons we have to confine our discussion to areas that have
received insufficient public attention or in which we have something new
to say. For example, since there are well-developed environmental and
wilderness movements, we have written very little about environmental
degradation or the destruction of wild nature, even though we consider
these to be highly important.

continually have to deceive themselves about their own motives and find
moral explanations for feelings and actions that in reality have a
non-moral origin. We use the term "oversocialized" to describe such
people. [2]
26. Oversocialization can lead to low self-esteem, a sense of
powerlessness, defeatism, guilt, etc. One of the most important means by
which our society socializes children is by making them feel ashamed of
behavior or speech that is contrary to society's expectations. If this is
overdone, or if a particular child is especially susceptible to such
feelings, he ends by feeling ashamed of HIMSELF. Moreover the thought and
the behavior of the oversocialized person are more restricted by society's
expectations than are those of the lightly socialized person. The majority
of people engage in a significant amount of naughty behavior. They lie,
they commit petty thefts, they break traffic laws, they goof off at work,
they hate someone, they say spiteful things or they use some underhanded
trick to get ahead of the other guy. The oversocialized person cannot do
these things, or if he does do them he generates in himself a sense of
shame and self-hatred. The oversocialized person cannot even experience,
without guilt, thoughts or feelings that are contrary to the accepted
morality; he cannot think "unclean" thoughts. And socialization is not
just a matter of morality; we are socialized to conform to many norms of
behavior that do not fall under the heading of morality. Thus the
oversocialized person is kept on a psychological leash and spends his life
running on rails that society has laid down for him. In many
oversocialized people this results in a sense of constraint and
powerlessness that can be a severe hardship. We suggest that
oversocialization is among the more serious cruelties that human beings
inflict on one another.
27. We argue that a very important and influential segment of the modern
left is oversocialized and that their oversocialization is of great
importance in determining the direction of modern leftism. Leftists of the
oversocialized type tend to be intellectuals or members of the
upper-middle class. Notice that university intellectuals [3] constitute
the most highly socialized segment of our society and also the most
left-wing segment.
28. The leftist of the oversocialized type tries to get off his
psychological leash and assert his autonomy by rebelling. But usually he
is not strong enough to rebel against the most basic values of society.
Generally speaking, the goals of today's leftists are NOT in conflict with
the accepted morality. On the contrary, the left takes an accepted moral
principle, adopts it as its own, and then accuses mainstream society of
violating that principle. Examples: racial equality, equality of the
sexes, helping poor people, peace as opposed to war, nonviolence
generally, freedom of expression, kindness to animals. More fundamentally,
the duty of the individual to serve society and the duty of society to
take care of the individual. All these have been deeply rooted values of
our society (or at least of its middle and upper classes [4] for a long
time. These values are explicitly or implicitly expressed or presupposed
in most of the material presented to us by the mainstream communications
media and the educational system. Leftists, especially those of the
oversocialized type, usually do not rebel against these principles but
justify their hostility to society by claiming (with some degree of truth)
that society is not living up to these principles.
29. Here is an illustration of the way in which the oversocialized leftist
shows his real attachment to the conventional attitudes of our society
while pretending to be in rebellion against it. Many leftists push for
affirmative action, for moving black people into high-prestige jobs, for
improved education in black schools and more money for such schools; the
way of life of the black "underclass" they regard as a social disgrace.
They want to integrate the black man into the system, make him a business
executive, a lawyer, a scientist just like upper-middle-class white
people. The leftists will reply that the last thing they want is to make
the black man into a copy of the white man; instead, they want to preserve
African American culture. But in what does this preservation of African
American culture consist? It can hardly consist in anything more than
eating black-style food, listening to black-style music, wearing
black-style clothing and going to a black-style church or mosque. In other
words, it can express itself only in superficial matters. In all ESSENTIAL
respects most leftists of the oversocialized type want to make the black
man conform to white, middle-class ideals. They want to make him study
technical subjects, become an executive or a scientist, spend his life
climbing the status ladder to prove that black people are as good as
white. They want to make black fathers "responsible," they want black
gangs to become nonviolent, etc. But these are exactly the values of the
industrial-technological system. The system couldn't care less what kind
of music a man listens to, what kind of clothes he wears or what religion
he believes in as long as he studies in school, holds a respectable job,
climbs the status ladder, is a "responsible" parent, is nonviolent and so
forth. In effect, however much he may deny it, the oversocialized leftist
wants to integrate the black man into the system and make him adopt its
values.
30. We certainly do not claim that leftists, even of the oversocialized
type, NEVER rebel against the fundamental values of our society. Clearly
they sometimes do. Some oversocialized leftists have gone so far as to
rebel against one of modern society's most important principles by
engaging in physical violence. By their own account, violence is for them
a form of "liberation." In other words, by committing violence they break
through the psychological restraints that have been trained into them.
Because they are oversocialized these restraints have been more confining
for them than for others; hence their need to break free of them. But they
usually justify their rebellion in terms of mainstream values. If they
engage in violence they claim to be fighting against racism or the like.
31. We realize that many objections could be raised to the foregoing
thumbnail sketch of leftist psychology. The real situation is complex, and
anything like a complete description of it would take several volumes even
if the necessary data were available. We claim only to have indicated very
roughly the two most important tendencies in the psychology of modern
leftism.
32. The problems of the leftist are indicative of the problems of our
society as a whole. Low self-esteem, depressive tendencies and defeatism
are not restricted to the left. Though they are especially noticeable in
the left, they are widespread in our society. And today's society tries to
socialize us to a greater extent than any previous society. We are even
told by experts how to eat, how to exercise, how to make love, how to
raise our kids and so forth.


THE POWER PROCESS

33. Human beings have a need (probably based in biology) for something
that we will call the "power process." This is closely related to the need
for power (which is widely recognized) but is not quite the same thing.
The power process has four elements. The three most clear-cut of these we
call goal, effort and attainment of goal. (Everyone needs to have goals
whose attainment requires effort, and needs to succeed in attaining at
least some of his goals.) The fourth element is more difficult to define
and may not be necessary for everyone. We call it autonomy and will
discuss it later (paragraphs 42-44).
34. Consider the hypothetical case of a man who can have anything he wants
just by wishing for it. Such a man has power, but he will develop serious
psychological problems. At first he will have a lot of fun, but by and by
he will become acutely bored and demoralized. Eventually he may become
clinically depressed. History shows that leisured aristocracies tend to
become decadent. This is not true of fighting aristocracies that have to
struggle to maintain their power. But leisured, secure aristocracies that
have no need to exert themselves usually become bored, hedonistic and
demoralized, even though they have power. This shows that power is not
enough. One must have goals toward which to exercise one's power.
35. Everyone has goals; if nothing else, to obtain the physical
necessities of life: food, water and whatever clothing and shelter are
made necessary by the climate. But the leisured aristocrat obtains these
things without effort. Hence his boredom and demoralization.
36. Nonattainment of important goals results in death if the goals are
physical necessities, and in frustration if nonattainment of the goals is
compatible with survival. Consistent failure to attain goals throughout
life results in defeatism, low self-esteem or depression.
37, Thus, in order to avoid serious psychological problems, a human being
needs goals whose attainment requires effort, and he must have a
reasonable rate of success in attaining his goals.


SURROGATE ACTIVITIES

38. But not every leisured aristocrat becomes bored and demoralized. For
example, the emperor Hirohito, instead of sinking into decadent hedonism,
devoted himself to marine biology, a field in which he became
distinguished. When people do not have to exert themselves to satisfy
their physical needs they often set up artificial goals for themselves. In
many cases they then pursue these goals with the same energy and emotional
involvement that they otherwise would have put into the search for
physical necessities. Thus the aristocrats of the Roman Empire had their
literary pretensions; many European aristocrats a few centuries ago
invested tremendous time and energy in hunting, though they certainly
didn't need the meat; other aristocracies have competed for status through
elaborate displays of wealth; and a few aristocrats, like Hirohito, have
turned to science.
39. We use the term "surrogate activity" to designate an activity that is
directed toward an artificial goal that people set up for themselves
merely in order to have some goal to work toward, or let us say, merely
for the sake of the "fulfillment" that they get from pursuing the goal.
Here is a rule of thumb for the identification of surrogate activities.
Given a person who devotes much time and energy to the pursuit of goal X,
ask yourself this: If he had to devote most of his time and energy to
satisfying his biological needs, and if that effort required him to use
his physical and mental faculties in a varied and interesting way, would
he feel seriously deprived because he did not attain goal X? If the answer
is no, then the person's pursuit of goal X is a surrogate activity.
Hirohito's studies in marine biology clearly constituted a surrogate
activity, since it is pretty certain that if Hirohito had had to spend his
time working at interesting non-scientific tasks in order to obtain the
necessities of life, he would not have felt deprived because he didn't
know all about the anatomy and life-cycles of marine animals. On the other
hand the pursuit of sex and love (for example) is not a surrogate
activity, because most people, even if their existence were otherwise
satisfactory, would feel deprived if they passed their lives without ever
having a relationship with a member of the opposite sex. (But pursuit of
an excessive amount of sex, more than one really needs, can be a surrogate
activity.)
40. In modern industrial society only minimal effort is necessary to
satisfy one's physical needs. It is enough to go through a training
program to acquire some petty technical skill, then come to work on time
and exert the very modest effort needed to hold a job. The only
requirements are a moderate amount of intelligence and, most of all,
simple OBEDIENCE. If one has those, society takes care of one from cradle
to grave. (Yes, there is an underclass that cannot take the physical
necessities for granted, but we are speaking here of mainstream society.)
Thus it is not surprising that modern society is full of surrogate
activities. These include scientific work, athletic achievement,
humanitarian work, artistic and literary creation, climbing the corporate
ladder, acquisition of money and material goods far beyond the point at
which they cease to give any additional physical satisfaction, and social
activism when it addresses issues that are not important for the activist
personally, as in the case of white activists who work for the rights of
nonwhite minorities. These are not always PURE surrogate activities, since
for many people they may be motivated in part by needs other than the need
to have some goal to pursue. Scientific work may be motivated in part by a
drive for prestige, artistic creation by a need to express feelings,
militant social activism by hostility. But for most people who pursue
them, these activities are in large part surrogate activities. For
example, the majority of scientists will probably agree that the
"fulfillment" they get from their work is more important than the money
and prestige they earn.
41. For many if not most people, surrogate activities are less satisfying
than the pursuit of real goals (that is, goals that people would want to
attain even if their need for the power process were already fulfilled).
One indication of this is the fact that, in many or most cases, people who
are deeply involved in surrogate activities are never satisfied, never at
rest. Thus the money-maker constantly strives for more and more wealth.
The scientist no sooner solves one problem than he moves on to the next.
The long-distance runner drives himself to run always farther and faster.
Many people who pursue surrogate activities will say that they get far
more fulfillment from these activities than they do from the "mundane"
business of satisfying their biological needs, but that is because in our
society the effort needed to satisfy the biological needs has been reduced
to triviality. More importantly, in our society people do not satisfy
their biological needs AUTONOMOUSLY but by functioning as parts of an
immense social machine. In contrast, people generally have a great deal of
autonomy in pursuing their surrogate activities.

TO BE CON...

Michael Eilers wrote:
>

> bb748@FreeNet.Carleton.CA (Milton Kleim) wrote:
> 
> > INDUSTRIAL SOCIETY AND ITS FUTURE

> >    for the human race. They have greatly increased the life-expectancy of
> >    those of us who live in "advanced" countries, but they have
> >    destabilized society, have made life unfulfilling, have subjected
> >    human beings to indignities, have led to widespread psychological
> >    suffering (in the Third World to physical suffering as well) and have
> >    inflicted severe damage on the natural world. The continued
> >    development of technology will worsen the situation. It will certainly
> >    subject human beings to greater indignities and inflict greater damage
> >    on the natural world, it will probably lead to greater social
> >    disruption and psychological suffering, and it may lead to increased
> >    physical suffering even in "advanced" countries.
> 
> This starts poorly. Not only it is mainly obfuscation, but he states a
> series of personal opinions as fact, not a particularly strong foundation
> to build his case upon. To claim that our current condition of unhappiness
> and angst is the direct result of the industrial revolution is to assume
> that there was a happier time somewhere in our past. History says
> otherwise. Would Dr. Kaczynski be as happy as a Russian peasant serf under
> the Tzars, crippled by hard labor and dead at 35 from anthrax? Or as a
> Zulu warrior (an agrarian hunter-gatherer society, stone-age technology)
> where the murder rate was 10 times modern levels and the battles raged for
> decades? Or be a medival peasant and get run through by a barbaian's blade
> smeared with pig shit? In fact, to claim that the present level of the
> world's fortunes is *lower* than it has been in the past is sheer
> arrogance--it is insulting to the people of the past, who have *really*
> suffered. 
> 
> THE UNUCRITIC

True, old forms of GOVERNMENT were oppressive, class segregated, etc.  But
revolutions and new governments are not dependent on technology.  Modern
democracy could afford us all life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness
with or without light bulbs, television sets, and SCUD missiles.  My
grandparents went without alot of the conveniences I have today, and yet
they tell me the world used to be a better place than it is today.  Hell,
maybe if we weren't all so concerned about TV's and cellular phones and
bigger and better weapons, we could feed and shelter the poor and the
homeless, and talk to our neighbors instead of clicking our garage door
openers from the safety of our cars, sanitarily shutting out everything
that doesn't come into our house on cables.  

Don't get me wrong, I love my computer.  I love the internet.  But I'd
give it all up to make the world a better place.  Wouldn't you?

Random Q. Hacker

body:
[Since this group is getting real good lately, I threw together a
 FAQ in hopes of cutting down on repetitive questions so the rest
 of us don't lose momentum.  Can anyone provide good revolutionary
 URLs to add to this? -Ric]


                        FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS(FAQ)
                                       
                              alt.fan.unabomber

   ---FAQ BEGINS---

   Last updated: May 5, 1996
   Author: ricardo@paranoia.com (Ricardo H. Gonzalez)
   http://www.paranoia.com/~ricardo/fc.html
   
   NOTICE: This text may not be reproduced in any form for profit without
   the permission of the author. It may be reproduced in any form
   provided that no money is being charged.
   
Index

   1. What is the purpose of this newsgroup?
   
   2. What does FC stand for?
   
   3. You are a strong supporter of FC. Are you a fed?
   
   4. If you are so against technology then why do you use the Internet?
   
   5. You seem to like nature, protecting the environment, and supporting
   free speech while disliking pollution, domination of society by
   business interests, and conformity to arbitrary societal values. Are
   the fans and supporters of FC really leftists?
   
   6. You seem to like rationality, fairly obtained success, and fighting
   for justice while disliking weakness, inferiority, and collectivism.
   Are the fans and supporters of FC really conservatives?
   
   7. If you're not left-wing or right-wing then what is your political
   position? Don't you have to be one or the other?
   
   8. Dr. Ted Kaczynski wasn't a productive citizen of society. So why
   listen to him?
   
   9. What is the connection between FC and environmental groups like
   Earth First?
   
   10. Where can I find the Manifesto?
   
   11. Don't you think FC should be ignored for resorting to violence to
   make themselves heard?
   
   12. What do you revolutionaries plan to do exactly?
   
   Online Resources

---BEGIN FAQ---

  1. What is the purpose of this newsgroup?
   
   The newsgroup alt.fan.unabomber exists for "fans of the mystical and
   awe-inspiring UNABOMBER" to discuss matters related to topics
   mentioned in its charter, including FC, their Manifesto, and
   revolution.
   
   This newsgroup name reflects the media mangling of a single FBI
   suspect who has eluded them for over 17 years and is possibly a member
   of the revolutionary group FC, which has an unknown number of members.
   The FBI suspect known as UNABOM was dubbed "The Unabomber" by the
   media because the media can sell more advertising for their newspapers
   and television programs when they inflate a story, introduce fictional
   elements, and provide a oversimplified one-dimensional perspective
   that misses the meaning of the event entirely. Since they are
   interested in providing entertainment for ratings and care little
   about provoking thought or seeking truth, the media will do everything
   possible to increase their ratings and persuade audiences to depend on
   their viewpoints.
   
   For the remainder of this FAQ, we will refer to "The Unabomber" as FC,
   for the group that he belongs to. This group authored the Manifesto
   entitled Industrial_Society_and_its_Future that will be referred to
   throughout this FAQ. While the suspect is unknown, the group has
   claimed responsibility for the actions that the FBI has attributed to
   this single individual.
   
   This group does not exist to:
   
       a) Condemn the actions of FC because of their supposed lack of
       contributions to society. Their Manifesto is a work of sheer
       genius that may prove to be the force that will save humanity from
       its devolution.
       
       b) Condemn the actions of FC because they did not conform to the
       arbitrary values of a passive society.
       
       c) Spread media propaganda about "Unabomber suspects," though the
       method of propaganda used by the media can be discussed and
       exposed.
  

  2. What does FC stand for?
  
   FBI officials for a long while suspected that the initials FC that
   were carved on FC's bombs stood for "Fuck Computers" but this is
   incorrect. The FBI later realized that FC has explained that the
   initials stood for "Freedom Club" in one of many letters that they had
   sent.
   
   It is unknown how many people are members of FC, but some have
   suggested that thousands of people individually share the basic ideas
   expressed in the Manifesto and are working towards similar goals. Some
   people have suggested that revolutionaries working toward the same
   goals as FC should consider themselves part of the organization.
   
   
  3. You are a strong supporter of FC. Are you a fed?
   
   I am not a fed. I am an interested ex-scholar who believes in the
   right to free speech, and in exercising my constitutional right I
   often side with the ideas of FC and defend FC against foolish
   criticisms. However, the threat of feds tying to entrap people is very
   real, so I suggest several guidelines for the safety of FC fans,
   members, and others who are disgusted by recent social trends and wish
   to spread new, more intelligent values. This information is intended
   mostly for audiences in the United States because so far there has
   been less interest in FC and their Manifesto from other areas of the
   world.
   
       a) Do not openly organize revolutionary efforts on the Internet. All
       Internet traffic is monitored at the major hubs by the government
       (mae-east, mae-west, fixed-east, and fixed-west have been
       confirmed as fully monitored and logged and newer net hubs are
       likely the same way. Assume that all email is intercepted and
       logged forever.
       
       b) Public posts are also logged, and not only by the government
       (search for your name on USENET archives kept at
       http://www.dejanews.com and http://altavista.digital.com if
       you've posted articles previously). If a current or potential
       employer runs your name through one of these services and doesn't
       like your opinions, you might run into problems.
       
       c) PGP is ok for exchanging basic information, but the computing
       power of the future will allow brute force attacks in a decade or
       two. If you use it, assume that your message will be read by
       others at some point in the future. Also make sure to use a
       2048-bit key or larger if you have a hacked version of the PGP
       software.
       
       d) To further the revolution, it is best that you work alone or
       with people that you have known a long time and can trust with
       your life. Do not work with someone you found on the Internet
       because they could be feds trying to entrap you, no matter how
       much you think you could trust them. Even exchanging ideas with
       another person could lead to implicating you in crimes that you
       are innocent of, so be careful even when discussing ideas with
       others.
       
       e) "Anonymous" remailers aren't necessarily anonymous and can't
       always be trusted. Since the feds can monitor all major network
       connections, they can see when you use a service like the one at
       anon.penet.fi because your message goes through at least one of
       their hubs on its way to Finland and it is trivial for them to see
       your message with full headers before it reached the anonymous
       service. Better methods are one-way chains of remailers if you
       want to post to USENET or send a fellow revolutionary advice.
       
   For more information on anonymity and cryptography you can read the
   Cypherpunks page at
   
   http://nic.funet.fi/pub/unix/security/crypt/cypherpunks/Home.html
   
   You may also want to read newsgroups such as alt.privacy,
   alt.privacy.anon-server, alt.privacy.clipper, and
   comp.society.privacy.
   
   If you are comfortable with the feds monitoring you and feel that this
   cause is important enough that you should participate in the
   discussion, then it is ok to use your name, but be warned of the
   possible dangers. Just be sure to refrain from offering information
   which is too specific or could implicate you in anything.
   
   
  4. If you are so against technology then why do you use the Internet?
   
   This question appears almost every week and seems to come only from
   people who have not read the Manifesto and understand it only
   superficially from what the media has told them about it. The short
   answer is that we are using the Internet to communicate with other
   revolutionaries and to spread the message of FC to others who are
   disenfranchised with the strangle hold of the system. We agree that
   technology is powerful, especially methods of communication, and we
   are using these powerful technologies solely as weapons to weaken and
   ultimately destroy the system.
   
   As FC wrote in the Manifesto:
   
   202. It would be hopeless for revolutionaries to try to attack the
       system without using SOME modern technology. If nothing else they
       must use the communications media to spread their message. But
       they should use modern technology for ONE purpose: to attack the
       technological system.
       
   
  5. You seem to like nature, protecting the environment, and supporting free
  speech while disliking pollution, domination of society by business
  interests, and conformity to arbitrary societal values. Are the fans and
  supporters of FC really leftists?
   
   Fans and supporters of FC rarely identify with one of the two
   mainstream parties. Most of us dislike the leftists and see them as
   harmful for many reasons, including their "feelings of inferiority"
   and "oversocialization." Paragraphs 6 - 32 and 213 - 230 discuss FC's
   position on this in detail.
   
   "Political correctness" has been a disaster for society because it has
   eliminated certain ideas from being acceptable for discussion. The
   left has decided that it didn't want people to think and communicate
   about things it doesn't like and declared that these ideas were
   improper. The left is only for free speech when it is not dominant and
   is rapidly fascist when it is dominant. This alone makes the leftist
   movement unacceptable to anyone who supports freedom.
   
   The leftist of old had several appealing ideas when they were not
   dominant, but they turned out to be worse than their opponents when
   they gain power.
   
   It is safe to assume that the vast majority of FC fans and supporters
   are not leftists.
   
   
  6. You seem to like rationality, fairly obtained success, and fighting for
  justice while disliking weakness, inferiority, and collectivism. Are the fans
  and supporters of FC really conservatives?
   
   Fans and supporters of FC rarely identify with one of the two
   mainstream parties. Most of us dislike modern conservatives and see
   them as harmful for many reasons, including their forced submission of
   individual rights to business rights, blind support of "progress" and
   the technoindustrial system, and dogma towards old, antiquated methods
   for dealing with new problems they have inflicted on society. While
   these topics are addressed throughout the Manifesto, there is a
   paragraph directed at the conservatives.
   
   50. The conservatives are fools: They whine about the decay of
       traditional values, yet they enthusiastically support
       technological progress and economic growth. Apparently it never
       occurs to them that you can't make rapid, drastic changes in the
       technology and the economy of a society without causing rapid
       changes in all other aspects of the society as well, and that such
       rapid changes inevitably break down traditional values.
       
   We note that conservatism used to mean individual freedom and limited
   government control over people's lives. While modern conservatism in
   the United States includes a good deal of government control over
   freedoms, including the prohibition of "consensual crimes" and forced
   acceptance of governmental morals (both of which are largely based on
   Christian roots), it also creates an environment where business
   dictates how government is run. This means that the proletariat are
   merely cogs in the machine who can have their freedoms removed if it
   would serve business better. For example, look at the hysteria of the
   drug war. While educated people understand the parallels with the
   first Prohibition (when was the last time you heard of someone killed
   over alcohol - when it was illegal) and that most drug users keep to
   themselves, the great fear from business is that people will use drugs
   and will lose interest in their mindless jobs and not be as productive
   as possible.
   
   Conservatives claim to be for less government control and less
   interference with people's private affairs but these claims are only
   true as long as people are doing things that are in accordance with
   the conservative's values. As soon as people start wanting these
   freedoms for their individual rights instead of as business rights (or
   as human machines for business), they find that this great
   conservative promise of freedom does not apply to them.
   
   It is safe to assume that the vast majority of FC fans and supporters
   are not conservatives.
   
   
  7. If you're not left-wing or right-wing then what is your political
  position? Don't you have to be one or the other?
   
   Most of the fans of FC don't but the idea of a two-party dictatorship
   wherein all citizens are supposed to believe in the ideas of one of
   the two parties. We find this concept to be far too limiting. We also
   find both parties to be in error in most of their decisions. However,
   the political process of appealing to herd values is largely to blame
   for this. Politicians are generally not interested in addressing
   legitimate problems and prefer instead to do whatever will gain them
   the most public support. There are few politicians who have genuine
   concern over the problems they face and for that reason and their
   general ineptness and stupidity, we oppose the two-party system they
   have created.
   
   Some supporters of FC are libertarians, though because of their pledge
   to never impose force on other people, they oppose FC's occasionally
   violent methods. Apparently is never occurs to them that revolution is
   often accompanied by violence because the oppressors who are the root
   causes of social stresses will not relinquish their positions of power
   without being violently overthrown by the proletariat. But because
   these people are interested in similar reforms to gain autonomy we
   gladly work with them, though some of the supporters of FC are not at
   all interested in political positions beyond reducing the amount of
   government control in our lives.
   
   Some supporters of FC are members of the Green party, which is most
   active in environmental issues. While the danger of dealing with
   leftist is possible, the benefit of being involved with this sort of
   party is that you can meet many enlightened individuals who are
   interested in achieving the same goals. The position on technology
   also varies with some believing that technology is the only way to fix
   the damage inflicted by the technoindustrial system and others
   thinking that widespread support for Green issues will allow nature to
   heal itself.
   
   
  8. Dr. Ted Kaczynski wasn't a productive citizen of society. So why listen to
  him?
  
   [Dr. Kaczynski is the latest FBI suspect in the "Unabomber crimes" but
   this in no way means that he was the Unabomber, a member of FC, or the
   author of the Manifesto.]
   
   This question most frequently is asked by people who have been
   oversocialized and believe that everyone must serve society in some
   way. These people believe that everyone should perform their 40-hour
   work weeks involved in a surrogate activity so that workers can earn
   money to provide for their nuclear family while making the company
   owner more wealthy in the process. People who make this argument do
   not seem to have great tolerance for others who aren't eager to
   conform to this model of societal behavior.
   
   The most obvious response is that there is no law that someone must be
   a "productive" citizen and spend the majority of their waking hours
   working. Wouldn't it make more sense to do what you wanted to do all
   day instead of what your boss wanted? The relevance of Dr. Kaczynski
   to this discussion is that he was a hermit who lived on very little
   money and spent his time expanding his intellect instead of doing
   pointless work for a company. This was his choice for a lifestyle,
   which he adopted after resigning from being a Berkeley professor.
   Since there is no reason to expect others to work for your society,
   there is no basis for disliking someone for their lack of contribution
   to it in the manner that you would prefer.
   
   Historically, many authors and artists have dropped out from the
   working world so they can dedicate themselves to developing their
   skills and producing work which often pays little or nothing and is
   not recognized as genius until after their deaths. People today who
   have great spirits often find themselves beaten down by the stress of
   modern work environments and society and are forced to make a
   difficult decision between letting their natural abilities fade or
   quitting their jobs to tap the energies and talents of their
   abilities.
   
   If Dr. Kaczynski is the author of the Manifesto, it could be said that
   he was much more productive than most citizens because of his ability
   to start a dialog about important topics and inspire revolutionaries
   to wage war against a broken system that is held together with
   delusions and empty promises. If he is the author, then we owe him a
   great deal of gratitude and respect for his work.
   
   
  9. What is the connection between FC and environmental groups like Earth
  First?
   
   While FC has strong environmental concerns, they have no link to
   groups like Earth First. While many fans and supporters of FC support
   the efforts of environmental groups such as Earth First, these groups
   are largely composed of leftist collectivists and are opposed for this
   reason.
   
   214. [...] A movement that exalts nature and opposes technology must
       take a resolutely anti-leftist stance and must avoid all
       collaborations with leftists. Leftism is in the long run
       inconsistent with wild nature, with human freedom and with the
       elimination of modern technology. Leftism is collectivist: it
       seeks to bind together the entire world (both nature and the human
       race) into a unified whole. But this implies management of nature
       and of human life by organized society, and it requires advanced
       technology. You can't have a united world without rapid
       transportation and communication, you can't make all people love
       one another without sophisticated psychological techniques, you
       can't have a "planned society" without the necessary technological
       base. Above all, leftism is drive by the need for power, and the
       leftist seeks power on a collective basis, through identification
       with a mass movement or an organization. Leftism is unlikely to
       ever give up technology, because technology is too valuable a
       source of collective power.
   
   For this reason, Earth First is an organization to avoid though on the
   surface it appears to share a few positions with FC.
   
   
  10. Where can I find the Manifesto?
  
   The Manifesto is online in several locations, including the UNAPACK
   page at http://www.paranoia.com/unapack/
   
   Serious fans may want to purchase a softcover version of the Manifesto
   from Jolly Roger Press, a Berkeley publisher. This is available at
   Tower Records or directly from the publisher.
   
   Jolly Roger Press
   P.O. Box 295
   Berkeley, CA 94701
   
   
  11. Don't you think FC should be ignored for resorting to violence to make
  themselves heard?
  
   The answer to this question requires the discussion of several related
   topics. For the first section we will quote FC from the Manifesto.
   
   96. [...] Anyone who has a little money can have something printed, or
       can distribute it on the Internet or in some such way, but what he
       has to say will be swamped by the vast volume of material put out
       by the media, hence it will have no practical effect. To make an
       impression on society with words is therefore almost impossible
       for most individuals and small groups. Take us (FC) for example.
       If we had never done anything violent and had submitted the
       present writings to a publisher, they probably would not have been
       accepted. If they had been accepted and published, they probably
       would not have attracted many readers, because it's more fun to
       watch the entertainment put out by the media than to read a sober
       essay. Even if these writings had had many readers, most of these
       readers would soon have forgotten what they had read as their
       minds were flooded by the mass of material to which the media
       expose them. In order to get our message before the public with
       some chance of making a lasting impression, we've had to kill
       people.
       
   Some oversocialized people will say that violence is wrong and that
   using freedom of speech is the best way to change problems in our
   society. However, this is flawed because few people today are willing
   to listen to intelligent, reasoned conversation and either hold
   tightly to their own preconceived notions about the way society should
   function and what individual rights are deserved. Others are
   uninterested in discussion of a rational nature because thinking is
   either difficult for them or causes boredom because of withdrawal from
   the entertainment media stimulus they are accustomed to. While people
   can certainly freely discuss their views, others rarely listen or
   respond to them, so freedom of speech is often of no use. In the
   spirit of being "open-minded" others simply disregard opinions with
   which they do not already agree.
   
   Since authority has traditionally used violence to keep others down,
   it seems fair that violence can be used against them to gain back
   freedom and autonomy.
   
   FC's dedication to their beliefs is certainly admirable in a time when
   few people stand for anything consistently. This is especially true
   when our society is exerting continuous pressure to conform, be
   passive, and refrain from confronting threats to one's lifestyle or
   freedom. While we are forced to walk the plank a step away from pure
   apathy, groups like FC who stand up for freedom are should be
   supported. FC's reasoning can be summarized in the following
   approximation: actions produce change, talk produces no change.
  

  12. What do you revolutionaries plan to do exactly?
  
   Most of us who are committed to changing the harm we see in society
   are not going to disclose our plans, but our intentions are fairly
   obvious. You might read about our work in newspapers and maybe your
   grandchildren will read about them in history books, but you'll
   probably see little offered in the newsgroup about our plans because
   that would be harmful to the revolution. A basic overview of some
   methods we will use is available in paragraphs 180 - 206.

body:
THE VERDICT IS IN
     
Two paperback books have already been written about the UNABOM matter 
and the suspect Ted Kaczynski.  The winner by a nose in the race to the 
bookstores was Mad Genius:  The Odyssey, Pursuit, and Capture of the 
Unabomber Suspect.  It was written by the "award-winning journalists" 
and the Editorial Staff of Time Magazine.  Close behind was Unabomber:  
On the Trail Of America's Most-Wanted Serial Killer, which was written 
by former FBI profiler John Douglas and co-author Mark Olshaker.  Both 
books are fair summaries of the facts reported by the press to date.  
Mad Genius is more readable, while Unabomber has the advantage of being 
written by someone who once was involved in the investigation.   Both 
books are impressive efforts to summarize complex facts in less than two 
weeks.   Whether -- given a man's liberty at stake -- it was something 
that needed doing is another matter.  


The beginning of both books requires the reader to keep the faith and 
read on.   Mad Genius begins with an essay on the paranoiac personality.  
Although most people would agree that the Unabomber is a deeply troubled 
individual, "paranoiac" is not necessarily a word that comes to mind.   
Many view the Unabomber as both supremely rational and patently immoral.  
Similarly, Unabomber begins with a lengthy description of the original 
"Mad Bomber" case in New York City nearly a half-century ago -- it is 
clearly an attempt to demonstrate the value of profiling.  The account 
might have been more persuasive if the authors had left out the part 
where the psychiatrist gleaned from the bomber's "W's" that he lived 
with a female relative who reminded him of his mother. 
         
Neither book contains material information not previously reported.  
Unabomber represents a greater departure from previous press reports in 
that it discusses the profiling done by one of the authors.  Some 
readers (and perhaps some members of the Task Force) may be annoyed at 
author John Hunter's self-congratulatory tone.  Douglas has previously 
faulted the FBI's probe in interviews in the press.  The author argues 
that the bomber might have been caught sooner if they had just heeded 
his view (and apparently that of other profilers) that the bomber was 
more intelligent and educated than thought.   Some members of the Task 
Force, Douglas suggests, persisted in focusing on speculation that the 
bomber was a blue collar worker in the airline industry.  "Had anyone 
asked me, I wouldn't have agreed with this."  Hindsight is indeed 20/20 
  Douglas' "retrospective" psychological insights provided in the 
appendix are truly that -- gleaned with the benefit of the accumulating 
evidence against suspect Kaczynski.

Both books borrow extensively from quotes previously reported in other 
press accounts.  Neither account, however, contains the most telling  
quote.  Department of Justice spokesman Carl Stern said:  "There are 
times when we try informally to prevent something which is grossly 
untrue from being published or broadcast, but in this case  I felt I 
couldn't do even that."
      
Mad Genius has a useful list of the 700+ items found in the shed.  The 
list contains some interesting items details not previously reported -- 
some of which appear to be highly incriminating.  For example, one can 
of screws apparently contained a handwritten note that read:  "burned 
and soaked in corroding solution -- clean."  The list includes a hooded 
jacket and zippered sweatshirt that were found; one was blue and the 
other was green.   Neither book emphasizes the fact that the witness 
reported a man in a gray hooded sweatshirt -- an unfortunate lapse given 
that the headlines featured the discovery of a hooded sweathsirt and 
sunglasses as if it were dramatic evidence confirming Kaczynski's guilt. 

Unabomber contains separate sections detailing the chronology of the 
Unabom incidents and the letters written by the Unabomber.  Both 
sections are correct in their facts.    Connections are drawn to 
Kaczynski, however, only where the perceived connection is corroborative 
of his guilt.  With respect to the November 1979 and June 1980 bombings 
that were mailed from the Chicago area, no mention is made of the fact 
that, by all accounts, Kaczynski had moved to Montana in the Summer of 
1979.  And some of the alleged connections are not persuasive -- for 
example,  in connection with an April 24, 1996 bombing, the authors note

includes a chapter titled "A Second Opinion," which quotes a behavioral 
analysis based, in part, on an examination of handwriting that is

nowhere allude to whether they view the "Nathan R" note as being in

matter, the  greatest strength of Douglas' book is his apt comments on

technology be eliminated, Douglas writes:

"Let's be real, here, folks.  He knows that isn't going to happen.  ...

inadequacies."  

As "true crime" books,  the books without a doubt prove that the man 
living in the shed was Theodore John Kaczynski.   Moreover, it appears 
clear that he had bomb-making materials in his possession.   They may 
even provide ample evidence that he was a clever and careful mailbomber.

the Unabomber, however, the books suffer the same drawback as the press 
reports.  We still do not know which of the press leaks are accurate.

was little doubt in the public mind that he and the Unabomber were one 
and the same."  This is an ironic statement for these influential 
journalists to make.  Only passing mention is made of the many grossly 
inaccurate headlines that pummelled readers in early and mid April.

screamed "Typewriter bombshell."   The reports were proved wrong when 
the lab tests did not confirm the agents' initial reported impressions 
that one of the two typewriters matched the one used to type the 
manifesto.   At about the same time that the disappointing lab tests

for which the final lab tests have not been announced.

by unnamed sources are flat out wrong.   

The Unabomber book actually repeats a number of apparently mistaken news

first reported by the Washington Post and then nationwide concerning a 
list of names of approximately 25 University of California-Berkeley 
mathematics professors allegedly found in the cabin.  Douglas and author 
Olshaker repeated the report even though the Post, along with most other 
major newspapers, had long since forthrightly explained that the report 
was wrong.  A campus policeman had mistakenly assumed that a handwritten 
list written by an FBI agent for his own purposes had been by the mad 
bomber. Similarly, he authors repeated the apparently unconfirmed 
reports that Kaczynski's family had purchased tickets to California (as 
opposed to have given Kaczynski money).  Finally, unlike Mad Genius, the

proprietors of Royal Hotel in Sacramento that he had stayed at their

variation used by many literate and educated folks.  And it is the more 
logical phrasing -- it is only remarkable if you think you can still 
have your cake after you eat it.  By definition, you need to have it 
before you can eat it.

types enlisted by his former colleague, Clint Van Zandt, is also 
disappointing.  Those experts relied upon only five pages of writing

and brother.  We could make authors Douglas and Olshaker look like any

yet know the exact contents of the  five pages were provided,  an expert 
might have demanded all available copies before rendering an opinion.  
Certainly, an opinion that a one of several hundred million people in 
this country was 60-80 percent likely to be a serial murderer should not 
have been given without seeing all available letters.  There are several 
authors on the usnet group "alt.fan.unabomber" ("Bandit" and "Ric 
Ricardo" to name two) who sound more like the Unabomber than Ted likely 
did in the five pages provided Van Zandt's  experts).

conclude that the note "Wu, I told you it would work . R.V." was a 
reference to two Berkeley math professors.   The conclusion (whether 
true or not)  is far less likely once one realizes that the handwritten 
list of math professors was, in fact, not found in the cabin.  Mad 
Genius is not without its curious statements and conclusions.  For 
example, the authors in Mad Genius summarily conclude that the same note 
attached to a 1982 bomb was "probably inadvertently" left by the bomber.

and was intended to mislead the Task Force. 

Both books make the same error that press reports have been making since 
April of last year -- the bomber, according to the conventional wisdom, 
was jealous of the attention paid to the Oklahoma City bombings.  The 
Oklahoma City bombing was April 19.  The Unabomber sent a sophisticated 
bomb on April 20 along with some fairly lengthy letters.  One of those 
letters announced that he had a lengthy manifesto (and he gave the 
approximate word count) that he would be forwarding.  It is unlikely 
that the bomber woke up on April 19 and after hearing of the explosion 
in Oklahoma said: "Boy, I'm glad I brought this typewriter to California 
with me on the bus so I could send out these letters and type these 
labels." 
        
Mad Genius shows a greater willingness to state the facts in ways that 
depart from the previous accounts.  For example, the journalist-authors 
boldly (and probably correctly) report that 22 people were injured 
rather than the 23 usually recited in the UNABOM folklore.  It was 
probably the psychology professor in 1985 that they didn't count.  He 
was merely standing by as his teaching assistant who opened the package, 
and was not, in fact, injured.  More significantly, Mad Genius casts a 
healthy dose of skepticism on a report by a man in Salt Lake City that 
he stayed at the same hotel as Kaczynski in 1978.  The fellow, now a 
karate instructor, is still waiting to keep the pompous bomber in a dark 
alley.  And to the author's credit, they raise a collective eyebrow at 
the report by the owner of the Sacramento hotel who, they note, "was 
less sure of himself when talking to investigators." 

Unabomber, however, is not without its advantages.  Not only are any 
errors of minor significance in the overall story, but the chronology 
and letters section (both of which bear an uncanny resemblance to the 
sections on a certain webpage),  serve as very useful guides in 
understanding the facts of the matter.  Moreover, Unabomber but not Mad 
Genius  includes the recent description by Professor Saari concerning 
his recollection that he had met Kaczynski, and that Kaczynski had vowed 
to get even after being treated rudely by engineering professors to whom 
Saari had referred him.  Finally, Unabomber, can easily lay claim to the 
best line: "Throughout the 1967 Summer of Love, Ted Kaczynski didn't 
have a single date."

Unabomber ends with a plea in favor of the significance of the type of 
psychological profiling done by the principal author.  One question, 
however, arises that has never been addressed by the authors or the 
press:  each week the public views the homicides presented in shows like  
NYPD Blue and Homicide.  Was the $50 million plus spent on this case 
worth it?  He hadn't made an attempt on an airline in nearly 15 years.  
It is not uncommon for several people to  die  on a given night in 
certain parts of our major urban centers.  Why, again, should we care 
about this particular murderer?

Any provable mistakes -- and there are factual inaccuracies in both 
books -- are truly minor given the wealth of detail that was summarized 
in such a short period.   On the most important issue of whether the 
manuscript was found, we can only wait to see if the leaks prove true.   

The conflicting accounts provided by these two books of the alleged 
discovery  demonstrate that such confidence may rest on a shaky 
foundation.  Mad Genius describes it as a carbon copy while Unabomber 
describes it as a "master" copy from which the Post and Time copies were 
typed.   A third view -- offered by a number of California papers -- is

it seems unlikely to have been a carbon copy.  And the draft sent to the 
Post and NY Times  apparently was identical even in its typographical 
mistakes, and so it seems unlikely to have been a "master" copy from

books and the press reports are wrong on this  point, might they be 
wrong altogether?  Might the draft have merely been a writing with an 
anti-technological theme?  Might the report in both books that a carbon 
copy of the letter to the New York Times was found also be mistaken?  
Finally, might the dramatic report of a handwritten "hit list" -- 
airline industry", "computer industry" and "genetecists" -- recounted 
only in Mad Genius be mistaken?  None of these critical pieces of 
evidence were detailed on the inventory of items taken from the cabin, 
even though it is quite detailed in other respects.

We will have to wait and see whether the evidence leaked by "sources 
close to the investigation"  bears up to scrutiny.  In the meantime, 
those interested in the UNABOM matter should go out and buy one or other 
of the books, and then be sure not to serve on the jury in any 
prosecution.
